paper.title: Algorithms for incomplete elliptic integrals (ACM TOMS Algorithm 577: RC, RF, RD, RJ; symmetric incomplete elliptic integrals)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 7(3), 1981, pp. 398-403; collected as TOMS Algorithm 577
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/577.gz (ACM article not read; ACM pages are not fetched here)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 577.gz, sha256 61ac0a82555128503bb1c0e7ad1b1911534377e0d1bb407a794579c4d2272c0e (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 into /tmp/scout-b2, read as text in /tmp/scout-b3/577, not executed).
code.note: Single Fortran file: four DOUBLE PRECISION subroutines (RC, RF, RD, RJ) followed by six test drivers. The RJ driver (the one whose comment block names the check value) sets ERRTOL = 1.D-3 and calls RJ(X,Y,Z,P,ERRTOL,IERR) for the sets it reads from stdin. Drivers print a table; they do not print an expected-value file. The check value is in the driver's comment, not in a separate .out file.

claim.location: Comment block of the RJ test driver inside 577.gz (the driver that follows the RF/RD drivers and reads X,Y,Z,P sets). Stated there: 'THE TWENTY-SECOND SET IS A CHECK VALUE: RJ(2,3,4,5) = 0.14297 57966 71567 53833 23308'. The input block of that driver (read on stdin, unit 5, 42 sets) has the 22nd set at file line 867: '2.00D+00 3.00D+00 4.00D+00 5.00D+00'. The routine must evaluate the integral numerically to produce its printed RJ value.

reference.file: 577.gz, the RJ driver's comment block (text inside the archive)
reference.sha256: not the member's own hash: scout's extracted text of the single file is /tmp/scout-b3/577/577.raw; rerun should read the archive member, not this copy

claim.metric: RJ(2,3,4,5), the Carlson symmetric elliptic integral of the third kind, as returned by the Algorithm 577 subroutine RJ called with ERRTOL = 1.D-3 from the RJ driver.
claim.paper_value: Shipped reference value 0.1429757966715675383323308 (the comment's 20 digits: 0.14297 57966 71567 53833 23308), read from the driver comment in the archive. The ACM article is not read here.

tolerance.basis: The driver sets ERRTOL = 1.D-3 and the subroutine comment says 'ERRTOL is set to the desired error tolerance', so the routine's accuracy contract is a relative error of ERRTOL on its result. Applied to the reference value, that is an absolute tolerance of 1.4297579667e-04 (1e-3 times 0.14297579667). Set before any run and not to be loosened after a run. A coding error that moves RJ(2,3,4,5) by more than one part in a thousand fails it; a rounding-level change does not.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute for the RJ driver's first sets; the build needs a Fortran compiler and no other tool.
cost.data_size: None; the input values are in the driver's data block.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS archive.

why: RJ(2,3,4,5) is a non-closed-form numerical value that the driver's own check comment gives to 20 digits, so the code has to run to reproduce it; the RC and RD check values in the same file are closed forms (pi, ln 2, lemniscate constants) and are not used as the claim.
